_doc: ch() scoping vectors (F435 W7, plan 'ch() scoping rules'). Written by item 7.B.
resolve: {name, from, path, expect}. 'from' is the id of the node whose code holds the call; expect is
{node_id, target} (target is a param name or an @attr) or null when the path leads nowhere. Paths start
at the calling node: '..' is the network it sits in, a name steps into that child, '/' is the root.
Resolution is structural: whether the node really has that param or writes that attribute is checked
later (ref_broken), so these vectors never depend on it.
rename: {name, rename: {node_id, new_name}, node_id, field, before, after}. field is 'code' or
'params.<name>' (an expression). After rename_node, the field of node_id reads 'after'.
cycles and assets are backend-only (they need compile): see test_ch_refs.py.

inner.name: inner
inner.code:
n = chi("../lookback")
m = chf("../sma/period")
k = chf("/vol/threshold")
# chf("../vol/threshold") stays: it is a comment
@w = ch("/sub/sma/@sma")

resolve.name: bare name: the calling node's own param
../name from a subnet child: a param of the enclosing network (promoted)
a root node is not a sibling of a subnet child
two levels up from a subnet child
relative path down into a network
a node that does not exist
an absolute name at the root
no target after the last slash
